clue.text: Ring number at place where actors may be filming

blocks.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
N is the standard abbreviation for number
a place or site

explanation.surface: A boxing ring is numbered as the spot where a film crew is shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' only joins wordplay to definition; 'place' does double service in the surface but is the last piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shot away from the studio, at a real site, is said to be made on location.

clue.text: Working towards the same goal, team gives forward support

blocks.note: on means onward, and also in favour of something, as in 'I'm on for it'
a side is a sporting team

explanation.surface: A football team backs up its centre-forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' and 'forward' push a football reading, but the definition is about cooperation, not the offside rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone onside is on your side, cooperating and committed to the same aim.

clue.text: Listen and learn, dean ordered

indicators.note: things that are ordered are put into a new sequence, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college dean instructs students to pay attention and study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen and learn' reads as one instruction, but only 'Listen' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for paying attention to what someone says.

clue.text: Reprimand fielders in unsuitable footwear for cricket

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to call them in for a telling-off
in cricket, slips are fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper, so fielders there are slippers

explanation.surface: Fielders are told off for turning up in the wrong shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close catching positions next to the wicketkeeper, so a fielder there can be called a slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft indoor house shoes would be useless on a cricket field, hence unsuitable footwear for the game.

clue.text: Tensed, screwed up?

blocks.note: first meaning: made taut or stiff
second meaning: screws turned further in, made more secure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' suggests ruined or anxious, but here it means a screw given extra turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a muscle drawn taut and a screw turned firmly home are described with the same past participle.

clue.text: Attack from the start

definitions.note: onset is the start; 'from the onset' is the sense

blocks.note: first meaning: an assault
second meaning: the beginning of something

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an instruction to go on the offensive straight away; it is two separate senses of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means both an assault and the beginning, as in the onset of winter.

clue.text: See start of Schneider Trophy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: An invitation to view the famous Schneider Trophy for seaplane racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Schneider Trophy was a seaplane air race; here the name only supplies an initial and the trophy becomes a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Pawn nobleman's precious stone

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A lord takes his jewel to the pawnbroker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' suggests hocking a gem, but it is the chess piece abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a gem formed in an oyster, loosely counted among precious stones.

clue.text: Bother about closing of station by NY borough

indicators.note: about suggests turning around or moving here and there, so the letters are scrambled
the closing of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the last letter of the word
by as in multiplied by, written with the times sign X

explanation.surface: Someone fusses about a station shutting down in a New York neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sign, as in 3 by 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronx is one of the five boroughs making up New York City.

clue.text: The groom may wait a moment

blocks.note: surface reading: a stable hand looks after riders' mounts while they are away
setter's reading: an exclamation telling someone to slow down and be patient

explanation.surface: A stable groom waits briefly while riders dismount.
explanation.walkthrough: A groom literally keeps hold of your mounts; the same words form the everyday exclamation urging patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiomatic cry asks someone to pause and not rush ahead, just like saying wait a moment.

clue.text: Device used by sailors on Ark Royal

indicators.note: the wanted letters are used by, held inside, the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found straddling the three words
surface padding, completing the name of the warship Ark Royal

explanation.surface: Kit carried by the crew of the aircraft carrier Ark Royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across sailorS ON ARk; 'Royal' just completes the name of the warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar is an underwater detection system that uses sound echoes, a device naval crews rely on.

clue.text: Boastful talk in front of groom as deacon prepared

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A deacon brags in front of the bridegroom while getting ready for the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons were proverbially boastful, hence the rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasconade is extravagant bragging, named after the supposedly boastful people of Gascony.

clue.text: Local lingo in citadel abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The speech heard inside a fortress in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' suggests foreign travel, but it signals the letters being spread about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, the speech of a particular area.

clue.text: Young child being led, trod awkwardly

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means doing it clumsily, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A little one taken by the hand stumbles along clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an &lit-style picture: a clumsily walking infant is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a child just learning to walk, typically aged one to three.

clue.text: Derogatory post in section of newspaper

blocks.note: personal remarks are rude ones aimed at an individual
a column is an upright pillar or post

explanation.surface: An insulting message posted in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests mail or an online comment; it is a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: The personal column is the part of a newspaper carrying private notices and messages from readers.

clue.text: Be eager to land in US naval base

blocks.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
to beach a boat is to bring it ashore

explanation.surface: Keen sailors wait to come ashore at an American navy port.
explanation.walkthrough: Long Beach in California long hosted a major US Navy base and shipyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Beach, California, was home to a large United States naval station and shipyard.

clue.text: Worldwide valuers in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it says to sort again into a different order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Property valuers are found in holiday towns across the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place; split as re-sort it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies everywhere, across the whole world.

clue.text: Refuse to entertain ICI functionary

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: offal can mean waste or rubbish, as well as edible innards
taken as written; ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British company

explanation.surface: Someone declines to host the chemicals firm ICI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning rubbish. ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a major British firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An official is a person holding an office, a functionary carrying out administrative duties.

clue.text: Such as dates that can't be kept?

definitions.text: Such as dates that can't be kept?

blocks.note: surface reading: social appointments that have to be cancelled
setter's reading: dates are a fruit, and these are ones you are not allowed to keep

explanation.surface: A list of appointments someone has had to cancel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dates are both engagements and fruit; fruit that may not be kept or enjoyed recalls the apple of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase names a tempting pleasure that is prohibited, and dates denied to you are prohibited fruit.

clue.text: Giving address, look round quiet church

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to see is to look
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
CH is a standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A speaker glances around a silent church while delivering a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' reads as a location but is a formal talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience, which is a speech.

clue.text: Trendy drink, one had by daughter in flat

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
a sip is a small drink
the Roman numeral for one
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter has a fashionable drink in her apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests a home, but it means dull or lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and insipid both describe food, drink or talk lacking flavour or liveliness.

clue.text: Indian lute, one carried by celebrity

indicators.note: what is carried by something is held within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a star is a famous person
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A famous musician lugs around a stringed instrument from India.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument of Indian classical music, a member of the lute family.

clue.text: 500 pixies endlessly dig

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
elves and pixies are both small mischievous fairies

explanation.surface: A huge band of fairies tirelessly excavating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' suggests digging without stopping, but it trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig, literally or in the sense of searching deeply.

clue.text: Audible cries of disapproval at college drinking spree

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: jeers from a crowd, which sound like a word for alcohol
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Students jeer loudly at a university event.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, a student in residence at Oxford or Cambridge is up, and one who leaves is sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is a British informal term for a session of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Among other things, bury one in a US city

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
LA is Los Angeles
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A funeral instruction to bury someone in an American city, among other tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: The one goes inside 'a LA', between the L and the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for among other things, used in formal writing.

clue.text: Woman with husband leaving Japanese dish, last of nine

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are removed
the last of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: sushi is vinegared rice with raw fish
H is the abbreviation for husband
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman's husband walks out of a Japanese restaurant at nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The H for husband is struck out of the dish before the final letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a female first name, and crosswords freely define names as woman or girl.

clue.text: Poet dropping in to play a prank

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so those letters go

blocks.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A poet calling in to fool around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like paying a visit; it means losing the letters of 'in'. Philip Larkin was a leading 20th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark or lark about is to fool around or play tricks.

clue.text: Behind me, a lush fumbled with the wine bottle

indicators.note: behind says the next pieces follow on after the named one
something fumbled is handled clumsily and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk behind the speaker clumsily grabs at the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A lush is a heavy drinker, which fits the surface but is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A methuselah is a large champagne or wine bottle holding eight standard bottles, named after the long-lived patriarch.
